features.claim: It had a long, low, narrow skull like a crocodile's.
features.quote: The skull of Spinosaurus was long, low, and narrow, similar to that of a modern crocodilian, and bore straight conical teeth with few to no serrations.

features.claim: Its teeth were straight, cone-shaped and smooth.
It had a long, muscular neck shaped like an S.
features.quote: As a spinosaurid, Spinosaurus would have had a long, muscular neck, curved in a sigmoid, or S-shape.

features.claim: It had big, strong front limbs with three-fingered hands and a big claw on the first finger.
features.quote: It would have had large, robust forelimbs bearing three-fingered hands, with an enlarged claw on the first digit.

features.claim: It had a sail on its back made of long spines.
features.quote: The distinctive neural spines of Spinosaurus, which were long extensions of the vertebrae, grew to at least 1.65 m (5.4 ft) long and were likely to have had skin connecting them, forming a sail-like structure.

features.claim: Its hip bones were small and its legs were very short for its body.
features.quote: The hip bones of Spinosaurus were reduced, and the legs were very short in proportion to the body.

features.claim: Its long, narrow tail was deep and shaped like a paddle.
features.quote: Its long and narrow tail was deepened by tall, thin neural spines and elongated chevrons, forming a paddle-like structure.

features.claim: It had a wide, paddle-like tail.
features.quote: It also had a wide, paddle-like tail.

features.claim: It had a narrow snout with a notch near the front of its jaws.
features.quote: Like other members of the spinosaur group, Spinosaurus had a narrow snout and a distinctive notch near the front of its jaws.

features.claim: It had a sail about 1.5 metres high on its back.
features.quote: There are several theories about the impressive 1.5-metre-high sail on Spinosaurus' back.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showed it as a land animal with long hind legs, which is wrong.
not_this.quote: For most of the last century scientists reconstructed Spinosaurus as a completely land-based animal with long hind legs, like Tyrannosaurus and Allosaurus.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showed it standing upright like other big theropods with a sail, which is out of date.
not_this.quote: After an influential 1955 skeletal reconstruction by Lapparent and Lavocat based on a 1936 diagram by Stromer, it has been treated as a generalized upright theropod, with a skull similar to that of other large theropods and a sail on its back, even having four-fingered hands.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showed it walking on all fours, but many scientists today think it walked on two legs.
not_this.quote: Some reconstructions of Spinosaurus show it walking on all fours, while many scientists today believe that it was able to walk on two legs.

debated.claim: Scientists are not sure whether it walked on two legs or on all fours.
debated.quote: It's still not clear who is right, and we may need to wait for new discoveries or studies to find out more.

second_reading.claim: Scientists are not sure whether it swam a lot or mostly lived on the shoreline.
second_reading.quote: It isn't clear whether this dinosaur swam a lot, or mostly lived on the shoreline.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists are not sure what the sail was for.
second_reading.quote: The function of the dinosaur's sail or hump is uncertain; scientists have proposed several hypotheses including heat regulation and display.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists are not sure whether it was mainly a land predator or a fish-eater.
second_reading.quote: It is unclear whether Spinosaurus was primarily a terrestrial predator or a piscivore, as indicated by its elongated jaws, conical teeth and raised nostrils.
